label: aicent-uri-grammar
text_status: the source is a published Internet-Draft, not agreed text of any working group: draft-li-rttp-iqa-addressing-02 is Informational and published for the public record
case_style: string-level: each case is a URI (or scheme-carrying string) and an expected grammar decision; the checker re-derives the decision from the ABNF and exclusions of the source text

sources.spec: draft-li-rttp-iqa-addressing-02, posted 2026-11-01, https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-li-rttp-iqa-addressing-02, sha256 02491c5a59d1e7471be04e8e0d4933dfc22ce19f9b054ead0aa449d6b4485044 of the retrieved TXT copy; sections 4.1 (Syntax) and 4.2 (Reserved Characters and Exclusions) are used

tightening_note: UG-N15 and UG-N16 carry status authoritative-tightening: the leading-hyphen rejection follows the author decision of 2026-11-09 and the -03 revision, not the literal ABNF of -02

cases.name: draft sec. 4.1 example, no action
cases.note: hash-intent (8 lowhex), no action; the default operation applies

cases.name: 8 non-lowhex letters parse as a name-intent
cases.note: 8 characters but 'g' and 'h' are outside lowhex, so the ABNF takes the name-intent branch; both forms are opaque to a client

cases.name: 8 lowhex digits parse as a hash-intent
cases.note: 8 lowhex digits take the hash-intent branch

cases.name: hyphens and digits inside every segment
cases.note: the segment set 1*( %x61-7A / DIGIT / "-" ) allows hyphens and digits in every segment and the action

cases.name: 7 hex-shaped characters are a plain name-intent
cases.note: only exactly 8 lowhex digits take the hash-intent branch; shorter hex-shaped labels are ordinary name-intents

cases.name: trailing hyphen in a segment (ABNF literal)
cases.note: 1*( ... / "-" ) admits a hyphen in any position including last; only the leading-hyphen position was tightened (author decision 2026-11-09, see UG-N15/UG-N16) - the -03 text will state this boundary explicitly

cases.name: uppercase intent is invalid input, not a formatting difference
cases.note: the canonical form is lowercase US-ASCII: a parser MUST NOT normalise it, because two distinct strings would then map onto one address

cases.name: uppercase scheme prefix
cases.note: the canonical form is lowercase US-ASCII and applies to the scheme too

cases.name: no rttps scheme and no fallback
cases.note: there is no "rttps" scheme and no fallback

cases.name: userinfo is not defined
cases.note: neither scheme defines userinfo, port, query or fragment; a URI carrying any of them is not valid

cases.name: fragment is not defined
cases.note: a fragment MUST NOT be used to address an action

cases.name: authority with two segments
cases.note: the authority is exactly three dot-separated segments

cases.name: empty middle segment
cases.note: each segment is 1*( ... ) and cannot be empty

cases.name: underscore is outside the segment set
cases.note: the segment set is %x61-7A / DIGIT / "-"

cases.name: second path segment
cases.note: the action is a single path segment

cases.name: empty action (trailing slash only)
cases.note: the action is "/" 1*( ... ) and needs at least one character

cases.name: leading whitespace before the scheme
cases.note: whitespace is not in any allowed set of the ABNF, in any position

cases.name: leading hyphen in the intent segment
cases.note: the sec. 4.1 ABNF literal 1*( %x61-7A / DIGIT / "-" ) admits a leading hyphen, but the published conformance vectors reject it; the -03 revision tightens the grammar accordingly (author decision 2026-11-09). Until -03 is posted this case tests the tightened reading, and a strict reading of -02 alone would score it unsettled

cases.name: leading hyphen in the pillar segment
cases.note: same tightening as UG-N15, applied to every segment position

cases.name: percent-encoded octet: MAY reject rather than normalise
cases.note: a canonical URI contains no percent-encoded octets, and a parser MAY reject such input rather than normalising it; both licensed decisions conform, so the case cannot be settled either way
